name: Canva
summary: Canva describes four parts to its hiring on its careers site: a recruiter Zoom call, a first interview with your potential coach (Canva's word for a manager) or a close collaborator, a take-home challenge you present back, and a final interview with close colleagues. Engineers usually skip the take-home and have a longer final interview mixing technical problem-solving with questions about their experience. Canva says the process usually takes four to five weeks and suggests answering with the STARR method.
rounds: Recruiter Zoom call about your experience and the role (engineers often get some technical questions here)
First interview with your potential coach or a close collaborator
Take-home challenge to complete in your own time and present back (most non-engineering roles)
Final interview: walk close colleagues through your challenge and answer behavioural questions; for engineers, a longer technical and experience interview
Decision, often within four to five weeks of the first call
looks_for: Skills from Canva's hiring framework for the role
Clear stories told with situation, task, action, result and reflection (STARR)
Craft and care in the work you show
How you explain your thinking to colleagues
Relevant skills, including ones from outside work

questions.text: Tell me about a project you're proud of. What did you do yourself, and what would you change now?
covers: The project and why it mattered
Your own decisions, separate from the team's
The result and a real reflection on what you'd change

questions.text: Tell me about a time you got feedback that changed how you work.
covers: The feedback and who gave it
What you changed, specifically
How you know the change worked

questions.text: Tell me about a time you helped a teammate succeed when it wasn't your job.
covers: What they needed and why you stepped in
What you did without taking over
What happened for them and the team

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to simplify something complicated for people who weren't experts.
covers: Who the audience was and what confused them
How you simplified it without losing what mattered
How you checked they understood

questions.text: Walk me through the take-home you did: what you chose to focus on, what you left out, and why.
covers: The goal you set from the brief
Trade-offs you made and the reasoning
What you'd do with more time

questions.text: How would you make a feature like a design template search feel fast for millions of people?
covers: What makes search feel fast: results, previews, caching
How you'd measure it and spot slow cases
Trade-offs between relevance and speed

questions.text: How would you decide whether a new editing feature is worth building for non-designers?
covers: Who it's for and the problem it solves
Signals and a small test before a full build
What success looks like and how you'd measure it

questions.text: Describe how you'd handle two teams wanting conflicting changes to a shared component.
covers: Understanding what each team actually needs
Options and their costs, written down
How you'd reach a decision and tell everyone

questions.text: Tell me about a piece of work where quality really mattered. How did you make sure it was right?
covers: Why quality mattered there
Checks, reviews or tests you used
What you caught and what slipped through

questions.text: How would you explain the impact of your last role to someone outside your field?
covers: The problem you worked on in plain words
One or two results with numbers if you have them
Why it mattered to the people it served

questions.text: Why Canva, and why this team?
covers: Something specific about Canva's product or mission that matters to you
How your skills fit this team's work
What you hope to learn

questions.text: What questions do you have for me about the team or the role?
covers: A question about how the team measures success
A question about the first few months
A question that shows you read about Canva

tips: Canva suggests the STARR method: situation, task, action, result and reflection. Prepare the reflection part; it's the one people skip.
For a take-home, present your reasoning and trade-offs, not just the final result.
Canva calls managers coaches; ask your first interviewer how the team works day to day.
Canva says its recruiters usually email from @canva.com addresses. Be wary of anyone using a personal email who claims to represent Canva.
